title: Ethiopian Dry Beef (Quanta)
community: All of Ethiopia — the sun-dried preserved beef tradition
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Quanta — beef marinated in berbere and mitmita, sun-dried for 2 days until preserved, then deep-fried in kibbeh until crispy. Ethiopia's ancient beef preservation technique — intensely spiced, chewy, extraordinarily flavourful dried beef that keeps for weeks.
longDesc: Quanta is Ethiopia's preserved beef tradition — strips of beef marinated in berbere and mitmita, dried in the highland sun for 2 days, then deep-fried in kibbeh until crispy and concentrated. The result is one of the most intensely flavoured beef preparations in the world — fiery, chewy, complex.
ingredients: 1 kg lean beef — sliced into thin strips 2—3cm wide
steps: Mix berbere, mitmita, salt, and 1 tbsp kibbeh.
Hang on a rack in direct sun for 2 days. Bring in at night.
The strips are ready when dry, stiff, and dark.
To cook: fry dried strips in hot kibbeh for 3—4 minutes per side until very crispy.
Eat as-is or use in Quanta Firfir.
chefTips: The drying must be complete — undried quanta does not keep.
The frying in kibbeh at the end adds the final layer of flavour.
Quanta keeps for weeks in an airtight container.
commonMistakes: Thick cuts — do not dry evenly.
cookingScience: See TZA075 and ETH015 for drying science. The berbere's acids and the salt act as additional preservatives alongside the dehydration — the combination of acid, salt, and moisture removal creates a multi-barrier preservation system.
sustainabilityTips: The most ancient food preservation technology — no energy, no refrigeration.
storage: Airtight container 3—4 weeks room temperature. Freeze 6 months.
culturalNote: Quanta is Ethiopia's ancient survival food — prepared before the long highland rainy season when travel is impossible, carried by traders and pilgrims across Ethiopia's mountains. Every Ethiopian grandmother knows how to make it; every Ethiopian child grows up eating it.
